html:
The Matsés, also called Mayoruna, and the Matis are two Panoan-speaking peoples of the Javari River basin, on the border between Peru and Brazil. Both are known for tattooed faces and for decorating their cheeks with thin sticks, like whiskers.

They live by hunting, fishing and farming manioc and plantains in the rainforest. During the rubber boom they kept away from outsiders and fought off intruders. Missionaries made lasting contact with the Matsés in Peru in 1969, and Brazilian officials met the Matis in the 1970s, after which disease killed many of them.

Today they live in large reserves in Peru and in the Javari Valley Indigenous Land of Brazil, next to the Korubo and the Marubo. See also Matsés.
